sections.normalized_html:
• A polynomial with one term is called a monomial. For example: [MATH: 1, \qquad y, \qquad 2x^3, \qquad 5a^{4}] However, the following expressions are not monomials because they can't be called polynomials: [MATH: \dfrac{1}{y}, \qquad 5t^{-1}, \qquad \sqrt{x}, \qquad 2z^{1/4}]

  • A polynomial with two terms is called a binomial. For example: [MATH: x+3, \qquad 7n^2 +n, \qquad p^{32} -1]

  • A polynomial with three terms is called a trinomial. For example: [MATH: z^2 -z +1, \qquad x^3 -2x -1, \qquad 2c^{4} - 3c^{3} +4c^2]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Polynomials with one, two, or three terms have special names.

Content:
- A polynomial with one term is called a monomial. For example:

However, the following expressions are not monomials because they can't be called polynomials:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{y},	\qquad	5t^{-1},	\qquad \sqrt{x}, \qquad 2z^{1/4}]
- A polynomial with two terms is called a binomial. For example:
[MATH: x+3,	\qquad	7n^2 +n,	\qquad	p^{32} -1]
- A polynomial with three terms is called a trinomial. For example:
[MATH: z^2 -z +1,	\qquad	x^3 -2x -1,	\qquad	2c^{4} - 3c^{3} +4c^2]
